blocks.text: Much of a newspaper article is made up of other people's words: statements, communications, sources. The journalist cannot bring them back without choosing a verb, and the verb is never neutral: "he said" , "he affirmed" , "he admitted" , "he sustained" , "he claimed" give to the same sentence a different weight. In this unit you systematically study the discourse reported in Arabic (statements, questions, orders), the scale of the verbs of attribution from the most neutral to the most burden of judgment, the types of source (declared, anonymous, concordant, social) and the way to make all this in English without losing or adding anything. It is the basic grammar of work on open sources. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-14.
